evidence: Narrowed candidate: resource-driven runtime adaptation for visual inspection on resource-constrained smartphones. 27 in-scope core papers (visual_inspection_scope Yes 20, Unknown 7). resource_awareness Yes 0 / No 4 / Unknown 23; adaptive_inference Yes 0 / No 4 / Unknown 23. Only P011 is a verified smartphone visual-inspection paper, and it is coded No for both runtime fields.
evidence_level: verified_full_text (P011, P015, P016, P020); abstract_only (remaining in-scope records)
counterexamples: No full counterexample in corpus; P011 partial; P029, P031, P033, P034 outside visual-inspection scope
limitations: The observation rests on four verified No records and a single verified smartphone visual-inspection paper.

evidence: 22 of 27 in-scope records are unresolved for the combination; each runtime field is Unknown for 23 of 27. P001 (smartphone, abstract only) is Unknown for visual inspection and both runtime fields.
limitations: Abstracts rarely state whether inference adapts at runtime, so the Unknowns are not evidence of absence. Resolving P001 to Yes would create a full counterexample.

evidence: Targeted searches S01–S08 and S17 found no full counterexample. Two researcher-confirmed partial counterexamples show adaptive inference in edge visual inspection: arXiv 2608.14727 (content-driven cascade on a Jetson Nano; adaptive_inference Yes, resource_awareness No under Decision A) and PMC11435656 (confidence-triggered edge-to-cloud escalation on a Raspberry Pi 4; resource_awareness Unknown). Neither runs on a smartphone, and neither establishes resource-driven adaptation.
supporting_papers: arXiv 2603.20288 (static; not a counterexample); PMC12074420 (not inspection)
counterexamples: partial: arXiv 2608.14727; PMC11435656. potential: Electronics 15(17):3915 (snippet only)
limitations: The searches were one page per query, access-limited, and designed against the pre-correction wording. The partial counterexamples weaken any broad adaptive-inference claim; the narrowed candidate (resource-driven adaptation on resource-constrained smartphones) is not eliminated by them.

evidence: PROJECT_SPEC.md names hardware/resource monitoring to dynamically adapt inference workloads, the adaptation/ and monitoring/ modules, and Phase 3 (resource adaptation policies).
limitations: Alignment with the project is not evidence about the literature.

evidence: Requires an Android phone, lightweight inspection models (e.g. MobileNet-class) and a runtime controller. Smartphone runtime-adaptation methods outside inspection (P029, P033, P034) show the mechanism is implementable on phones.
limitations: Assumes access to at least one Android device and no heavy model training without approval (AGENTS.md). Device diversity is limited.

evidence: Latency, CPU/GPU load, memory, battery level and thermal status are exposed by Android APIs (e.g. thermal status, BatteryManager). The corpus papers that measured runtime adaptation on phones (P029, P031, P033, P034) did so on device.
limitations: Assumption: vendor-specific counters vary in accuracy. The API details are not part of the verified corpus and need confirming on the target device.

evidence: Public optical inspection datasets used by verified papers include MVTec AD and VisA (arXiv 2603.20288, 2410.11591) and PCB defect sets (PMC11435656). 3D-print datasets appear in P015 and P016. Phone-captured data for a 3D-print scenario would need collecting.
limitations: Public datasets are not captured on phones. Runtime adaptation needs streams or sequences, not only still images.

evidence: Controlled conditions (static vs. adaptive policy, induced load or thermal stress, fixed scenes) can be scripted on one device. The verified smartphone adaptation papers use such protocols.
limitations: Ambient temperature, background processes and OS throttling policies are confounders. Repetitions are needed.

evidence: Static (non-adaptive) deployment is a natural baseline, as used by P011 and by the edge papers. Published adaptive comparators exist outside inspection (P029, P033, P034).
limitations: Comparators come from other tasks, so their numbers are not directly comparable.

evidence: The adaptation trigger (resource signal), the adaptation action (model or resolution switch) and the policy can each be disabled or fixed independently.
limitations: Proposed idea; not demonstrated in this project yet.

evidence: Accuracy, latency, throughput, energy proxies and thermal state are standard quantities in the verified related work (P029, P031, P034; arXiv 2309.00022 measures energy with a power meter).
limitations: Inspection accuracy under adaptation needs a task-appropriate metric (e.g. defect recall at fixed false-alarm rate).

evidence: Needs an on-device inference runtime, several model variants, a telemetry reader and a policy. This matches planned modules (inference/, adaptation/, monitoring/) but none is implemented yet (Phase 1).
limitations: Android integration is Phase 4 in the roadmap.

evidence: Could support a measured study of resource-driven runtime adaptation for a smartphone inspection task, with an explicit static baseline. Verified outside-scope work shows the mechanism exists, so any contribution would concern the inspection setting and its evaluation, not the mechanism itself.
limitations: Depth depends on whether inspection-specific behaviour differs from general vision workloads. That is a hypothesis, not established.

evidence: Verified related work appears in mobile-systems and embedded venues (MobiCom: P029; DAC: P031; ACM TECS: P033; IEEE TMC: P034) and in industrial-inspection venues (Information Fusion: P011).
limitations: Venue fit is indicative only.

evidence: Narrowed candidate: direct joint energy and thermal evaluation of resource-adaptive visual inspection on resource-constrained smartphones. 27 in-scope core papers; energy_evaluation Yes 0 / No 4 / Unknown 23; thermal_evaluation Yes 0 / No 4 / Unknown 23; adaptive_inference and resource_awareness each Yes 0 / No 4 / Unknown 23. The four No values (P011, P015, P016, P020) come from full text. Every core paper coded Yes for energy or thermal (P006, P028, P029, P030, P031, P032, P034) is outside the visual-inspection scope, and none of them is coded Yes for both.
evidence_level: verified_full_text (P011, P015, P016, P020); abstract_only (remaining in-scope records)
counterexamples: No full counterexample in corpus; P007 potential (energy and thermal Unknown)
limitations: Energy and thermal results are rarely stated in abstracts, so 23 Unknowns limit the observation.

evidence: 23 of 27 in-scope records are Unknown for energy and for thermal. P007 (edge, visual inspection) stays unresolved because its full text was inaccessible.
limitations: Full-text review of the in-scope edge papers is the main route to resolving these Unknowns.

evidence: Searches S09–S17 found no full counterexample. arXiv 2603.16451 (TinyGLASS) is a verified partial counterexample: in-sensor industrial visual anomaly detection (Sony IMX500 on Raspberry Pi 5) reporting 4.0 mJ per inference, but no thermal results and not on a smartphone. Six other edge visual-inspection papers were verified as having no energy or thermal results.
supporting_papers: arXiv 2603.20288; arXiv 2410.11591; arXiv 2606.07659; arXiv 2512.13497; arXiv 2608.14727; PMC11435656 (all: no energy or thermal results)
counterexamples: partial (researcher-confirmed): arXiv 2603.16451. potential: Electronics 15(17):3915; FOMO/Edge Impulse paper; P007
limitations: TinyGLASS (edge_device Yes, smartphone No under Decision C) shows energy evaluation of edge visual inspection outside the corpus, which weakens any broad edge/energy claim; this is why the candidate was narrowed. It does not establish joint energy + thermal evaluation, resource-adaptive inspection or a smartphone platform. Searches were designed against the pre-correction wording, so the joint/resource-adaptive form was not searched as one query.

evidence: PROJECT_SPEC.md lists thermal and energy-aware computing, thermal sustainability as an evaluation target, and the monitoring/ module (temperature, battery, power).
limitations: Alignment with the project is not evidence about the literature.

evidence: The narrowed candidate needs a phone, a resource-adaptive inspection workload (i.e. a GC-01-type adaptation mechanism) and a joint energy/thermal measurement method. arXiv 2309.00022 shows an external power-meter protocol on an edge device, and P031 measures thermal behaviour on a phone.
limitations: External power measurement of a phone usually needs battery bypass or a USB power monitor. Availability is an assumption.

evidence: Thermal state and battery level are readable on Android. Energy can be estimated from battery counters or measured externally. P029 and P034 report energy on mobile devices, and P031 reports thermal behaviour.
limitations: Battery-counter resolution and sampling rate vary by device. Software-only estimates have unknown error unless calibrated against an external meter.

evidence: Energy and thermal behaviour depend on the workload, not on labels, so public inspection datasets (MVTec AD, VisA, PCB sets) can drive the workload. Accuracy must still be reported alongside.
limitations: Continuous-capture realism (live camera vs. replayed images) changes the energy profile. arXiv 2608.14727 shows that the data path dominates wall time on an edge device.

evidence: Sustained-load runs with periodic sampling of temperature, throttling state and energy are practical. Warm-up and ambient control are required (arXiv 2608.14727 notes timing varies with thermal state).
limitations: Ambient temperature, phone case and charging state are confounders. Repeated runs are required.

evidence: Baselines can be measurement conditions rather than competing methods: model variants, precisions, frame rates and cloud offload. Published energy figures for edge visual inspection exist (arXiv 2603.16451) but on different hardware.
limitations: Cross-hardware energy numbers are not directly comparable.

evidence: Factors such as model size, precision, input resolution, frame rate and pre-filtering can be varied one at a time.
limitations: Proposed idea; ablation of a measurement study is factor variation, not component removal.

evidence: Energy per inference or per inspected part, average power, time to throttling and temperature trajectories are quantitative and used in verified work (P031; arXiv 2603.16451; arXiv 2309.00022).
limitations: Requires a documented measurement protocol to be reproducible.

evidence: A measurement harness and telemetry logging (monitoring/), an on-device inference path, and, because the narrowed candidate concerns resource-adaptive inspection, a runtime adaptation mechanism (adaptation/).
limitations: Narrowing to resource-adaptive inspection makes GC-02 depend on a GC-01-type mechanism. Hardware measurement setup, if external, adds practical complexity.

evidence: Supports an empirical characterisation (measurement study) of joint energy and thermal behaviour of resource-adaptive smartphone inspection. On its own this is an evaluation contribution rather than a method.
limitations: Depth is limited if results mainly reproduce known device behaviour. Whether inspection workloads behave differently is an untested hypothesis.

evidence: Verified related work appears in embedded and circuits venues (DAC: P031; AICAS 2026: arXiv 2603.16451) and mobile venues (P029, P034).
limitations: Venue fit is indicative only.

evidence: Narrowed candidate: an integrated resource-aware smartphone visual-inspection system combining runtime adaptation with confidence-aware downstream verification (five components: resource awareness; smartphone; visual inspection; runtime adaptation; confidence-aware verification). Within the 27 in-scope core papers, no paper satisfies three of the four Step 9.7 components (smartphone; visual inspection; runtime adaptation; confidence-aware downstream decision), and resource_awareness is Yes 0. confidence_gating is Yes 1 (P016, edge, not smartphone) / No 2 / Unknown 24. P011 has smartphone and visual inspection but No for adaptation and confidence gating.
counterexamples: No full or partial counterexample in corpus; P001 potential
limitations: The observation is assembled from separate components that are each sparsely coded, and it shares GC-01's thin smartphone evidence.

evidence: 22 of 27 in-scope records are unresolved for the combination. confidence_gating is Unknown for 24 of 27 (38 of 46 core papers), and the runtime fields for 23 of 27.
limitations: Confidence-triggered actions are seldom described in abstracts. This is the most Unknown-dependent of the three candidates.

evidence: Searches S18–S27 found no full counterexample. PMC11435656 meets three of four components outside the corpus: visual inspection, a per-sample runtime change of the computation path, and confidence-triggered escalation. It runs on Raspberry Pi 4 edge devices, not a smartphone, and is not resource-driven. ActiveInspect (Sensors 26(15):4932) selects additional views when evidence is ambiguous, but on A100 GPUs with a learned policy. arXiv 2608.21967 describes uncertainty-based human referral that is not yet evaluated online.
supporting_papers: arXiv 2608.14727 (cascade, trigger not described as confidence)
counterexamples: partial (researcher-confirmed): PMC11435656; ActiveInspect (doi 10.3390/s26154932); arXiv 2608.14727. potential: arXiv 2608.21967; P001
limitations: Edge systems outside the corpus already combine adaptation, confidence-aware decisions and/or active view selection; this weakens any broad claim and is why the candidate was narrowed to the integrated resource-aware smartphone realization. Under Decision B, ActiveInspect's learned view selection is not counted as confidence gating (Unknown). PMC11435656 and ActiveInspect were keyword-scanned, not read end to end.

evidence: PROJECT_SPEC.md covers uncertainty-based flagging for human review (uncertainty/), multi-view inspection, quality pre-filtering (acquisition/quality) and resource adaptation (adaptation/), across Phases 2–3.
limitations: Alignment with the project is not evidence about the literature.

evidence: Combines the GC-01 requirements with a confidence-triggered action (recapture, additional view or referral). The individual mechanisms are demonstrated separately (P016 confidence gating; P029/P033/P034 adaptation; PMC11435656 edge escalation).
limitations: Interactive actions (recapture, additional view) need a user or rig in the loop, which complicates controlled evaluation.

evidence: Resource signals are measurable as for GC-01. Confidence-triggered actions are measurable as event rates (referral, recapture, additional-view rates) and their effect on accuracy.
limitations: Measuring user-driven recapture on a phone needs logging of user actions and timing. This is a proposed idea.

evidence: Confidence-triggered additional views need multi-view or re-captured data per object. Real-IAD-style multi-view datasets are used by ActiveInspect. Phone-captured multi-view or recapture sequences for 3D-printed parts would need collecting.
limitations: Pre-acquired pools (as in ActiveInspect) simulate, but do not reproduce, live recapture.

evidence: Possible with a fixed rig and scripted recapture or view changes. User-in-the-loop handling adds variability.
limitations: The effects of the adaptation and the gating interact, so factorial designs are needed. The sample sizes required are unknown.

evidence: Baselines: static model without gating; gating without adaptation; adaptation without gating. Published single-component comparators exist (P016 gating; PMC11435656 edge escalation; ActiveInspect view selection).
limitations: No published integrated smartphone comparator was found in these searches.

evidence: A factorial (adaptation on/off × gating on/off × action type) ablation is natural.
limitations: Proposed idea. The number of conditions grows quickly.

evidence: Accuracy, recall at a fixed review rate, referral/recapture rate, latency and resource use can all be quantified. ActiveInspect reports observation count against accuracy, and PMC11435656 reports edge/cloud detection results.
limitations: The trade-off between operator workload and accuracy needs an agreed operating point.

evidence: The highest of the three: the GC-01 stack plus a confidence/uncertainty component and an acquisition-feedback loop (app UI or rig).
limitations: Depends on Phase 3 and Phase 4 components that do not exist yet.

evidence: Admits a system-integration study with testable sub-questions (does gating compensate for adaptation-induced accuracy loss?). Verified edge work already integrates adaptation with confidence-triggered escalation, so depth would come from the smartphone setting and the resource-driven trigger.
limitations: The sub-questions are hypotheses. Integration studies can be judged as engineering unless the questions are made explicit.

evidence: Related verified work appears in sensor and industrial venues (Sensors: PMC11435656, ActiveInspect; Processes: P016; Information Fusion: P011).
limitations: Venue fit is indicative only.
